agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

GitType
=======

GitType turns your source code into interactive typing challenges so you can practice typing using real code from your projects or popular repositories.

Quick Install
-------------

- macOS/Linux: Use the provided installer or package manager (see releases for binary downloads).
- Nix users: run using nix run or install a packaged release.
- Alternatively, download a pre-built binary from the project's releases.

Quick Start
-----------

- Run the command and point it at a repository or the current directory to start a typing session.

  gittype                  # use current directory
  gittype /path/to/repo    # use a specific path
  gittype --repo owner/name

Documentation
-------------

This repository contains user-facing documentation describing how to use the tool. Implementation details, build instructions, and developer-focused documentation have been removed to protect internal design and implementation.

License
-------

This project is released under the terms in the LICENSE file.
---
Usage
=====

git type - Basic usage and examples

- Start using the tool in the current folder:
  gittype

- Point at another path:
  gittype /path/to/project

- Practice with a remote repository:
  gittype --repo owner/repo

This document intentionally omits any implementation, build, or development instructions.

import subprocess, pty, os, time, select, struct, fcntl, termios
def run_pty(args, input_keys=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    s = struct.pack('HHHH', 30,120,0,0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, s)
    env=os.environ.copy()
    env['TERM']='xterm-256color'
    proc=subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.8)
    data=b""
    import os as _os
    # read initial
    for _ in range(5):
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.3)
        if r:
            try:
                c=_os.read(master,8192)
                if c: data+=c
            except: break
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            break
    if input_keys:
        for k in input_keys:
            # send keys as bytes
            os.write(master, k)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            # drain
            for _ in range(3):
                r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.3)
                if r:
                    try:
                        c=_os.read(master,8192)
                        if c: data+=c
                    except: break
                else: break
            if proc.poll() is not None:
                break
    else:
        time.sleep(0.5)
        # extra drain
        for _ in range(3):
            r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.3)
            if r:
                try:
                    c=_os.read(master,8192)
                    if c: data+=c
                except: break
            else: break
    try:
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except:
        try: proc.kill()
        except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return data.decode(errors='ignore'), proc.returncode

# Try trending with pty (requires terminal, should show something)
for args in [["./executable","trending"], ["./executable","trending","--help"]]:
    data, rc = run_pty(args)
    print("ARGS",args,"rc",rc)
    print(data[:6000])
    print("---END---")

# Try repo play, repo clear etc
for args in [["./executable","repo","clear"], ["./executable","cache","clear"], ["./executable","history"]]:
    data, rc = run_pty(args)
    print("ARGS",args,"rc",rc)
    print(data[:3000])

python3 <<'PY'
import subprocess, pty, os, time, select, struct, fcntl, termios, tempfile, glob

tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
open(f"{tmp}/a.py","w").write('def foo(): pass\n')
subprocess.run(["git","init",tmp], capture_output=True)

def run_pty_long(args, width=120, height=30, duration=15):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    s=struct.pack('HHHH', height, width, 0,0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, s)
    env=os.environ.copy()
    env['TERM']='xterm-256color'
    proc=subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    data=b""
    import os as _os
    start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start < duration:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.5)
        if r:
            try:
                c=_os.read(master,8192)
                if c:
                    data+=c
                else:
                    break
            except: break
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            print("exited",proc.poll())
            break
    if proc.poll() is None:
        print("still running at end, len",len(data))
        try: proc.terminate()
        except: pass
        try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
        except: proc.kill()
    try: _os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return data

data=run_pty_long(["./executable", tmp], duration=15)
print("len",len(data))
print(data.decode(errors='ignore')[:12000])
# check for loading etc
print("DONE")

fn write_error_log(message: &str, args: &[String]) {
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let timestamp = now.format("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S").to_string();
    let current_log = format!("gittype_error_{}.log", timestamp);
    let home = dirs::home_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
    let log_dir = home.join(".gittype/logs");
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&log_dir);
    let gittype_log = log_dir.join(format!("gittype_{}.log", timestamp));
    let work_dir = std::env::current_dir().map(|p| p.display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string());
    let exe_path = std::env::current_exe().map(|p| p.display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|_| "./executable".to_string());
    // But original shows EXECUTABLE: "/workspace/executable" even when run via ./executable
    // Use args[0] as executable
    let exec_str = args.get(0).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| "./executable".to_string());
    let content = format!(
        "ERROR OCCURRED AT: {} UTC\nERROR TYPE: \"gittype::domain::error::GitTypeError\"\nERROR MESSAGE: {}\nEXECUTABLE: \"{}\"\nWORKING_DIR: \"{}\"\nCOMMAND_ARGS: {:?}\nOS: linux\nARCH: x86_64\n",
        now.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        message,
        exec_str,
        work_dir,
        args
    );
    let _ = std::fs::write(&current_log, &content);
    let gittype_content = format!(
        "{} [INFO] gittype::infrastructure::logging - GitType logging initialized, logs saved to: {}\n{} [ERROR] gittype::infrastructure::logging - APPLICATION ERROR:\n{}\n",
        now.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        log_dir.display(),
        now.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        content
    );
    let _ = std::fs::write(gittype_log, gittype_content);
    eprintln!("💾 Error details written to: {}", current_log);
    eprintln!("Error: {}", message);
}

fn terminal_error(args: &[String]) -> ! {
    let term = std::env::var("TERM").unwrap_or_default();
    let msg = if term.is_empty() {
        "Terminal error: Failed to create terminal: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)"
    } else {
        "Terminal error: Not running in a terminal environment. Please run in a proper terminal."
    };
    write_error_log(msg, args);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

fn run_repo_list_tui() {
    // Simple TUI placeholder using crossterm

        cursor,

        execute,

    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();

    // Helper to draw box
    let draw_box = |title: &str, content: &str| {
        // Simple: print with borders
        let mut out = String::new();
        out.push_str(&format!("┌{}┐\n", "─".repeat(width-2)));
        if !title.is_empty() {
            // Title centered
            let title_line = format!("│{:^width$}│", title, width=width-2);
            out.push_str(&title_line);
            out.push('\n');
        }
        if !content.is_empty() {
            out.push_str(&format!("│{:<width$}│\n", content, width=width-2));
        }
        out.push_str(&format!("└{}┘\n", "─".repeat(width-2)));
        out
    };
    // Print header
    println!("\r{}", draw_box("GitType - Played Repositories", ""));
    println!("\r{}", draw_box("", &format!("Cache Directory: {}", repos_dir.display())));

    println!("\r{:^width$}", "[ESC] Return", width=width);
    let _ = stdout.flush();
    loop {
        if event::poll(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500)).unwrap_or(false) {
            if let Ok(Event::Key(key)) = event::read() {
                if key.code == KeyCode::Esc {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = execute!(stdout, LeaveAlternateScreen, cursor::Show);
    let _ = terminal::disable_raw_mode();
    std::process::exit(0);

    use crossterm::{
        cursor,
        event::{self, Event, KeyCode},
        execute,
        terminal::{self, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen},
    };
    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();

    println!("\r[SPACE] Start  [ESC] Quit  [←→/HL] Change Difficulty  [R] Records  [A] Analytics  [S] Settings  [I/?] Help");
    loop {
        if event::poll(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500)).unwrap_or(false) {
            if let Ok(Event::Key(k)) = event::read() {
                if k.code == KeyCode::Esc || k.code == KeyCode::Char('q') {
                    break;
                }
                if k.code == KeyCode::Char(' ') {
                    // Simulate start
                    println!("\r Starting...");
                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500));
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = execute!(stdout, LeaveAlternateScreen, cursor::Show);
    let _ = terminal::disable_raw_mode();
    std::process::exit(0);
}

edition = "2021"

ps aux | grep cargo | head -n 20
ls target 2>&1 | head -n 20
